newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-LME daily stock reports hits at speculators.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-LME daily stock reports hits at speculators.

text.p: Local metals dealers said on Thursday a changeover to daily stock reporting at the London Metal Exchange (LME) would probably curtail some speculative trading in futures contracts.
The LME said on Wednesday it was to move to daily reporting of metals stocks beginning April 7 for an initial period of six months.
Stocks currently were made public only on Tuesdays and Fridays.
Market speculators and other investors frequently bought and sold metal in the run up to reports, betting prices would go up when stocks go down and vice-versa.
"It's probably a good thing," a dealer for an LME ring dealing member told Reuters.
"It means more information... More of an open market. You don't get those twice-weekly blips and things."
Another dealer said it would provide less opportunity for speculators to second-guess market sentiment.
"This will make it a bit harder to manipulate the market," he said.
Initial reaction from some others, though, had been that the LME was treading a fine line in offering more disclosure.
The move the daily stock reporting follows criticism of the LME about the disclosure of data in the wake of the multi-billion dollar Sumitomo corp copper trading scandal in 1996.
Other initiatives by the LME included disclosure of ownership of metal and mandatory reporting of large market positions.

It has been suggested that had the market been better informed of the dealings of rogue Sumitomo trader Yasuo Hamanaka over some 10 years, the scandal might have been avoided, or at the least its impact on world metals markets.

One dealer said the LME was running the risk of "making every day a Tuesday and Friday," with speculators taking daily views on stock levels. However, this scenario was less likely as stock levels would probably not move much on a daily basis, the dealer added.
